title: Kladdkaka
subtitle: Swedish sticky chocolate cake, crisp at the edges and gooey at the centre
excerpt: Kladdkaka is a Swedish chocolate cake baked so the edges are crisp and set while the centre stays almost molten. The batter is barely more than melted chocolate, butter, eggs, and sugar with just enough flour to give the edges structure. It is baked for exactly 12 to 14 minutes and served cold or at room temperature, dusted with icing sugar.
sourceNotes: Kladdkaka is a Swedish chocolate cake whose name translates roughly as sticky cake. Documented in Swedish cookbooks from the twentieth century and now a standard home-baking recipe across Scandinavia.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze whole, well wrapped, for up to 2 months. Thaw overnight at room temperature.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made the day before. Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 3 days.

content.text: Kladdkaka is a Swedish chocolate cake baked to be sticky and gooey in the middle with a crisp, papery crust over the edges. It uses minimal flour on purpose: the structure comes from the eggs rather than the flour, and the centre stays soft and almost fudgy even after cooling. Serve cold with a dusting of icing sugar.
The timing is critical. Two minutes too long and the middle sets completely; two minutes too short and it does not hold together for slicing. Start checking at 12 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180 degrees C (fan 160 degrees C / gas 4). Grease a 20 cm round cake tin and line the base with baking paper.
Melt the butter and chocolate together in a small saucepan over a very low heat, stirring until smooth. Remove from the heat and leave to cool for 5 minutes.
In a large bowl, whisk the eggs and caster sugar together for 2 minutes until pale and slightly thickened. Stir in the vanilla extract.
Pour the melted chocolate mixture into the egg and sugar mixture and stir to combine. Sift in the flour and cocoa powder and fold in until just combined. The batter is quite liquid.
Pour into the prepared tin. Bake for 12 to 14 minutes. The edges will look set and slightly cracking; the centre should still have a distinct wobble when you move the tin.
Leave to cool completely in the tin before removing. The centre will firm up as it cools but stays fudgy. Dust with icing sugar before serving.

attrs.problem: Centre completely set and the cake is more like a brownie than a kladdkaka
attrs.avoid: Avoid baking past the 14-minute mark if the oven runs at the correct temperature.
attrs.fix: Check your oven temperature with a thermometer. If the oven runs hot, reduce to 175 degrees C and check at 11 minutes.

attrs.problem: Cake collapsing in the middle when sliced before fully cold
attrs.avoid: Avoid slicing while the cake is still warm; the centre is liquid until it cools completely.
attrs.fix: Leave in the tin for at least 1 hour at room temperature. If in doubt, chill for 30 minutes in the fridge; the centre will be firmer but still gooey.
